sentences.text: Matter is taken up in the revised call.

By means of the the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No. 506 of 2023 at Police Station- Khandouli, District- Agra under Sections 498A, 304B, 302 I.P.C.
and Section 3/4 of DP Act.
The applicant is in jail since 23.12.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 03.05.2024.

The following arguments made by Sri Ajay Dubey, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Sri Chandan Agarwal, learned AGA-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:

sentences.text: 1. The applicant is the husband of the deceased.
2. The applicant never demanded dowry or harassed the deceased.
3. The applicant is bereaved by the death of his wife.
4. The applicant had a long working hours and often went out of city for work.
The deceased became depressed on account of separation from her husband.
5. The deceased was a temperamental lady who was prone to extreme reactions over trivial issues.
6. On the fateful day she succumbed to depression and took the extreme step of ending her life.
She committed suicide by hanging.
7. The postmortem report opines the cause of death as asphyxia due to antemortem hanging.

8. Injuries depicted in the postmortem report consistent with hanging are:
(i) Nature of ligature mark.
(ii) No abnormality was detected in the hyoid bone.
9. The applicant did not aid or abet the suicide.
10.

The P.W. 1 who is the first informant (father of the deceased) and P.W. 2 who is the brother-in-law of the first informant in their testimonies before the trial court have repudiated the prosecution case.
The said witnesses have been declared hostile at the instance of the prosecution.
11. The applicant is a law abiding citizen who cooperated with the police investigations and had joined the trial proceedings.
12. The applicant did not influence the witnesses or tamper with the evidence.
13. The applicant never adopted any dilatory tactics or impeded the process of the trial.
14. The trial has moved at an inordinately slow pace.
The applicant is not responsible for the delay in the trial.
15. Inordinate delay in concluding trial had has led to virtually an indefinite imprisonment of the applicant without there being any credible evidence to implicate him in the offence.
16. The right of the applicant to speedy trial has been violated.
Ashok vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38328614/

sentences.text: 2 17. The trial is not likely to conclude soon due to heavy docket of the trial court.
18. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from the instant case.
19. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Ashok be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii )
The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement rendered by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru.
Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. (Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the socioeconomic status of the applicant.
Order Date :- 14.8.2024 Dhananjai  Ashok vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38328614/
